summary: Spec is structurally sound but has two material gaps: AC-M6-6 contradicts current hook reality (5 existing functions already exceed 30 lines, so 'no violations reported' is unachievable without un-specified refactor), and E8 split-direction edge case has no AC despite being central to R4's per-metric rule.

evidence: pretool-quality-gate.py:19-21 declares MAX_FILE_LINES=800, MAX_FUNC_LINES=30, MAX_NESTING=3 as hard module-level constants
main() at lines 209-247 calls get_final_content() (post-only) and never reads pre-state
is_exempt() at line 34 is the only bypass mechanism — purely path/extension-based, no sentinel/env-var/delta logic
Lines 238-243: any non-empty post-state violations list triggers exit(2) regardless of pre-state
Hand-off doc (lines 32-79) independently confirms the absent mechanisms; 8 blocked edits inventoried

edge_case_analysis.edit_with_pre_state_no_metric_worsens: ALLOW — design correct (line 233 metric_did_not_worsen returns True)
edge_case_analysis.write_to_nonexistent_file_with_violation: BLOCK — design correct (get_pre_content returns '', falls through to emit_violations)
edge_case_analysis.write_overwriting_existing_compliant_fil: BLOCK — design correct (pre-state has no violations, post is new violation, metric_did_not_worsen returns False)
edge_case_analysis.edit_at_threshold_stays_at_threshold: ALLOW — design correct (post not in violations → early exit at 'if not post_violations: sys.exit(0)')
edge_case_analysis.edit_at_threshold_pushes_past: BLOCK — design correct (post triggers violation, pre had no violation → metric_did_not_worsen returns False)
edge_case_analysis.edit_function_grows_in_oversized_file: BLOCK — design correct (post[fn] > pre[fn] → returns False)
edge_case_analysis.edit_function_shrinks_but_file_grows: BLOCK — design correct (file_lines worsens → returns False)
edge_case_analysis.edit_pure_shrink: ALLOW — design correct (all metrics improve or unchanged)
edge_case_analysis.edit_function_renamed_same_size: FALSE BLOCK — bar(35) treated as new function > 30 → BLOCK. BA acknowledges in E4 ('bias: be strict on names that didn't exist before'). Acceptable but worth noting as a known false-positive.

concerns.issue: metric_did_not_worsen nesting comparator uses post['max_nesting'] <= max(pre['max_nesting'], MAX_NESTING) instead of the cleaner post <= pre. The max() formulation adds a special-case for 'post compliant' that is already covered by the early-exit on empty post_violations. Dev may implement as written and inadvertently introduce behavior beyond R4's plain reading of 'nesting depth after <= before'.
concerns.recommendation: BA should simplify to post['max_nesting'] <= pre['max_nesting'] OR explicitly justify the max() form.

ac_review.note: Pre-existing legacy + 1-line additive edit → allow. Falsifiable. Measurable (exit code + optional stderr). Aligns with M1/R1.
Function 35→40 in oversized file → block. Falsifiable. The numeric example differs from M2's '32→33' but both are valid 'growing function' cases. Acceptable.
Brand-new file with 31-line function → block. Tests R2 (no grandfathering for new code). Clear and falsifiable.

AC text correctly documents BOTH sub-cases (stays-at-800 → allow, goes-to-801 → block). However, the second sub-case is documented inline in a parenthetical rather than as a discrete sub-AC. Readable but not crisply enforceable; QA should require Dev to demonstrate BOTH cases.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION. AC says 'no violations are reported (file <= 800, every function <= 30, nesting <= 3)'. Current hook has 5 existing functions over 30 lines (check_function_length_python=43, check_function_length_ts=37, check_nesting_depth=37, get_final_content=32, main=39 — verified by line-counting). After Option α fix, hook running on itself would: (a) detect these existing violations, (b) read pre-state and find same violations, (c) grandfather → exit 0 with stderr. So 'exit 0' is achievable but 'no violations are reported' is FALSE. The spec is silent on whether Dev must refactor these 5 existing functions. Either AC-M6-6 must be amended to 'exits 0 (possibly with grandfathered stderr)' OR BA must explicitly add to 'files_to_modify' a directive to refactor those 5 functions.

missing_acs.case: E8 split-direction (function A shrinks, function B grows in same edit)
missing_acs.rationale: R4 explicitly demands per-metric / per-function comparison ('NOT a global aggregate'). E8 is the canonical test for this. Dev could implement metric_did_not_worsen as a global 'sum of violation severities' compare and pass all 6 ACs while silently violating R4. An AC mandating that B's growth blocks regardless of A's improvement is required.
missing_acs.recommendation: Add AC-M6-7: GIVEN file with two oversized functions A(35) and B(20). WHEN edit reduces A to 30 (improvement) AND grows B to 32 (new function-level violation). THEN hook exits 2.

evidence: Verified existing function lengths in pretool-quality-gate.py via wc/awk: 5 functions exceed 30 lines (43, 37, 37, 32, 39).
Current file is 251 lines (BA spec says 252 — off by one, trivial).
BA prescribes 3 new helpers each <=30 lines. Math: 251 + ~50 (helpers) + ~30 (collect_violations + emit_violations extracted from main) = ~330 lines. Well under 800. File-level OK.
BA explicitly requires extracting collect_violations and emit_violations from main, but is SILENT on the 5 already-oversized existing functions.
If Dev refactors all 5 existing oversized functions: AC-M6-6 strict reading passes, BUT diff is much larger than BA's 'minimal extension' framing implies.
If Dev only adds the 3 new helpers + extracts main helpers: file remains compliant in line-count, BUT the 5 existing oversized functions persist and AC-M6-6 strict reading fails.

concerns.issue: BA spec creates an unresolvable choice for Dev: respect AC-M6-6 strictly (refactor 5 existing functions) OR respect line 67's 'extend, NOT rewrite' constraint (leave existing functions). These cannot both be honored as written.
concerns.recommendation: BA must pick one: either (a) explicitly authorize refactor of the 5 existing functions and list them in scope/files_to_modify with target line counts, OR (b) amend AC-M6-6 to 'hook exits 0 when invoked on itself (grandfathered exit acceptable)' and accept that the meta-test does not require strict compliance of existing functions.

evidence: Novelty rationale at context.prior_attempts.novelty_check.rationale is correct: this is a structurally new approach (delta-aware decision) in a previously-untouched hook.
BA spec line 273 mandates sentinel check before Dev edits.

objections.location: AC-M6-6 (ba-spec line 197-202) vs current hook reality
objections.finding: AC-M6-6 demands 'no violations are reported' when hook scrutinizes itself. But 5 existing functions in pretool-quality-gate.py already exceed 30 lines (43/37/37/32/39). The Option α grandfathering will make exit code 0, but violations ARE reported on stderr. AC-M6-6 as written cannot be satisfied without refactoring those 5 existing functions, which is NOT in development_approach.files_to_modify scope or scope.included.
objections.recommendation: Amend AC-M6-6 to: 'WHEN the hook is invoked on its own file path with a no-op edit, THEN the hook exits 0 (with optional grandfathered stderr).' OR add to scope.included: 'Refactor existing oversized functions check_function_length_python, check_function_length_ts, check_nesting_depth, get_final_content, main to <= 30 lines each.'
objections.blocks: Dev will land a fix that either fails strict AC-M6-6 reading or expands scope beyond what BA authorized.

objections.finding: R4 mandates per-metric / per-function comparison ('NOT a global aggregate'). E8 (function A shrinks, function B grows) is documented in Edge Cases but has no AC. A buggy implementation that compares aggregate violation counts (e.g., post.violation_count <= pre.violation_count) would pass all 6 ACs while silently violating R4.
objections.recommendation: Add AC-M6-7: 'GIVEN file with functions foo (35 lines, violation) and bar (20 lines, OK). WHEN Edit reduces foo to 30 (clears its violation) and grows bar to 32 (new violation). THEN hook exits 2 with stderr listing bar's violation.' This forces per-function bookkeeping in metric_did_not_worsen.

objections.finding: The prescribed `post['max_nesting'] <= max(pre['max_nesting'], MAX_NESTING)` is more permissive than R4's plain text 'nesting depth after <= before'. The early-exit on empty post_violations already covers compliant post-states; the max() form is therefore unnecessary and adds reader confusion.
objections.recommendation: Simplify to `post['max_nesting'] <= pre['max_nesting']` to match R4 verbatim, or explicitly justify the asymmetry with file_lines and per-function compare (which use plain post <= pre).

objections.finding: AC-M6-4 packs two distinct test cases (stays-at-800 → allow; goes-to-801 → block) into one AC body via parenthetical clarification. Falsifiable but not crisply enforceable for QA.
objections.recommendation: Split into AC-M6-4a (at-threshold same-line edit → allow) and AC-M6-4b (at-threshold growth-by-1 → block). Minor improvement; not blocking.

summary_one_line: FAIL — AC-M6-6 contradicts hook's current 5-function pre-existing oversize state, and R4's per-function rule lacks a dedicated AC (E8 split-direction), so a global-aggregate buggy implementation could pass all 6 ACs.

refined_context.for_ba: Resolve OBJ-1 by either (a) amending AC-M6-6 wording to accept grandfathered exit-0, OR (b) adding refactor of 5 existing oversized functions to scope.included and files_to_modify. Add OBJ-2's AC-M6-7 to lock in per-function metric semantics. Optional: simplify metric_did_not_worsen nesting comparator (OBJ-3) and split AC-M6-4 (OBJ-4).
